author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory: veterinarians grouped by the specialty they hold
summary: A read-only inverse projection of the veterinarian directory: one un-paged page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it, and groups veterinarians holding no specialty under a no-specialty heading.
acceptance_criteria: Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then every specialty is listed by its stored name, each with the veterinarians who hold it shown by full name (first name then last name, e.g. "Helen Leary").
Given a veterinarian who holds no specialty, when the specialty directory is opened, then that veterinarian appears under a no-specialty grouping rather than under any named specialty.
Given the clinic's specialties, when the specialty directory is opened, then all of them render on a single page, with no pagination.
Given the new specialty page, when any page of the system is rendered, then it still carries navigation to owner search and to the veterinarian directory as REQ-SYS-001 requires (unchanged).
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged).

Adding a navigation link to the specialty directory from every page: not among the product owner's decisions. REQ-SYS-001 is left as written (owner search + veterinarian directory only); discoverability of the new page is an open question the slice does not depend on.
notes: Inverse projection of REQ-VET-001. Product owner specified the page is served at GET /specialties.html (route recorded here for design; kept out of the PRD narrative, which stays behavioral like REQ-VET-001). REQ-SYS-001 judgment: the new page inherits REQ-SYS-001's navigation requirement automatically (it is a page), so no wording change is needed; I deliberately did NOT widen REQ-SYS-001 to make every page link TO the specialty directory, as that was not decided.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Inverse read projection on the existing vet slice: controller -> VetRepository -> Thymeleaf, per the feature-package organization (system-design.md#package-structure, ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization). No new module, no cross-package dependency, no service layer. The load-bearing decision (authoritative specialty source, name ordering, no-specialty grouping) is recorded in ADR 2026-08-06-specialty-directory-projection and reflected in the VetController/VetRepository/Specialty rows of system-design.md#contracts. Basis is grep + Read, not the IDE oracle (not connected): VetController.java, VetRepository.java, Vet.java, Specialty.java read directly.
integration_points: Add a query method to VetRepository returning the authoritative specialty set ordered by stored name (SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name). Keeps the vet slice's single-repository shape and matches the prescribed file_targets; leave it uncached (do NOT add it to the 'vets' cache).

Add a GET /specialties.html handler to VetController that reads the specialty set (authoritative axis) plus the cached vetRepository.findAll() (holdings axis) and builds a per-specialty view model: each specialty -> its veterinarians by full name; a single no-specialty group for vets with getNrOfSpecialties()==0, placed after the named specialties and omitted when empty. Route recorded in the prd-entry notes.

New template templates/vets/specialtyList.html using th:replace layout fragment so it inherits the REQ-SYS-001 navigation (owner search + vet directory) automatically. Do NOT add a navbar link TO this page (prd-entry non-goal; REQ-SYS-001 not widened). Full name rendered first-then-last as the existing vetList does (vet.firstName + ' ' + vet.lastName).
VetControllerTests gains the three prd-entry test_names, driven via MockMvc against a MockitoBean VetRepository (existing pattern).

patterns.description: stable name-based ordering of specialties (Comparator.comparing(NamedEntity::getName)) — the same 'stable order' REQ-VET-001 edge case 1 asks for; binds this page identically: ordered by stored name, deterministic across requests, independent of HashSet iteration order
declarative Spring Data repository returning a lookup type in name order — the model for the authoritative specialty read
full-name rendering and the #{none} idiom for the no-specialty case; reuse #{specialties} for the heading

risks.risk: Deriving the projection from vet holdings alone (the simpler path) silently drops any specialty held by no veterinarian, contradicting 'every specialty the clinic knows'. Latent under current seed data (all three specialties are held), so it would pass the stated tests while breaching the requirement wording.
risks.mitigation: Enumerate from the specialties table (authoritative axis), not from vet associations. Recorded in ADR 2026-08-06-specialty-directory-projection; VetRepository specialty query is the primary path.

risks.risk: REQ-LANG-002 build-time test walks templates and compares all eleven locale bundles; any new user-facing message key that is not added to every bundle fails the build.
risks.mitigation: Reuse existing keys where possible (#{specialties} for the page heading, #{name}, #{none}); if a distinct no-specialty group label is needed, add the new key to all eleven message bundles.

risks.risk: The inversion/join logic lives in the controller, reinforcing the no-service-layer gap (Open Question 2).
risks.mitigation: Consistent with the project's current standing (ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization); do not introduce a service layer for this slice — that would contradict the established pattern. Neither improves nor worsens the recorded gap.

notes: Read-only GET, no mutation: no new CSRF/authz surface beyond the existing open-access posture; the page discloses only already-public vet and specialty data, same as /vets.html. Thymeleaf auto-escaping covers XSS on echoed names. Empty-collection edges render gracefully (empty/omitted groups). REQ-SYS-001 judgment matches the prd-entry: the page inherits navigation via the layout fragment; discoverability (a link TO it) is an out-of-scope open question. No design-doc-autofix records to audit.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: findSpecialties() uses a static parameterless JPQL literal (SELECT s FROM Specialty s ORDER BY s.name) with no concatenation or user input — no JPQL/SQL injection surface
GET /specialties.html accepts no request parameters, path variables, or user input; no tainted-data path reaches the query or view
Thymeleaf template escapes all echoed values via th:text (specialty names and vet full names); no th:utext or unescaped inlining, so no stored-XSS vector on directory-managed data
Endpoint discloses only specialty names and vet full names — the same data category already public via /vets.html; no PII, credentials, or data beyond the existing veterinarian directory
Read-only GET with the existing open-access posture; no state mutation, no new authz/CSRF surface
No dependency or build.gradle changes in this slice — no supply-chain/CVE exposure introduced

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: SpecialtyGroup is a static inner class that functions as an immutable value type but does not realize the value-object pattern. It lacks equals()/hashCode() and therefore uses reference equality from Object, violating the architecture-principles.md closed property 'equality by value'. The framework-entity exception does not apply: SpecialtyGroup is not a persistence entity and the framework does not instantiate it. Java records satisfy all three: immutability, structural equality, and the modern-Java-idioms checklist item. Spring Framework 6+ BeanWrapper resolves record accessor names (name(), veterinarians()) from Thymeleaf SpEL expressions like ${group.name}, so no template change is needed.
findings.fix: Replace the static inner class with a record: public record SpecialtyGroup(String name, List<Vet> veterinarians) {}. The Javadoc comment can move to the record's Javadoc. Remove the explicit constructor, field declarations, and getters.

findings.description: Reviewer reached planned checkpoint after reviewing 2 of 4 changed files (VetRepository.java and VetController.java). specialtyList.html and VetControllerTests.java have not yet been reviewed. Findings above cover VetRepository.java and VetController.java only.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Specialty list ordering is not tested. The test checks that 'radiology' and 'surgery' both appear via containsString, but asserts nothing about their order in the specialtyGroups model attribute. The ADR (2026-08-06-specialty-directory-projection.md) explicitly requires ordering by stored name, independent of hash-set iteration order. A regression that replaces the name-ordered specialties list with any non-deterministic enumeration would pass this test undetected.

Veterinarian ordering within a named specialty group is not tested. Every named-specialty scenario in the suite places at most one veterinarian under each specialty, so no test can detect a HashSet-iteration regression in the veterinariansHolding sort path. The ADR requires vets within each specialty to render in a deterministic name-based order; only the no-specialty group has an ordering assertion (specialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty). A second vet added under 'radiology' (e.g. Adams before Leary) with a contains(hasProperty...) assertion would cover this path.

All four new test method names omit the 'the' prefix required by the project naming school (testing-principles.md § Test Naming: 'the{Subject}Should{Outcome}'). Methods should be theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEachSpecialtyWithVeterinariansByFullName, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty, theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage, and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian. The brief applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward; these are all new.
findings.fix: Rename all four test methods to carry the 'the' prefix. The prd-entry test_names list omits the prefix too; update it in handoff.jsonl via a superseding prd-entry correction if the harness requires it, or treat the method rename alone as sufficient since test_names is advisory.

approved_aspects: specialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian correctly pins the specialty-authoritative behavior: it stubs findSpecialties() with dentistry+radiology but findAll() with only a radiology-holding vet, then asserts containsString('dentistry'). A vet-holdings-inverting implementation (ADR option 1) would not render dentistry at all, so this test would fail against it. The no-vet-per-specialty behavior is adequately pinned.

No-specialty group ordering is tested: specialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty supplies Baker and Adams deliberately out of alphabetical order, then asserts contains(hasProperty('lastName', is('Adams')), hasProperty('lastName', is('Baker'))), which is an order-sensitive assertion that would fail under HashSet iteration.
All three PRD acceptance criteria for REQ-VET-003 have dedicated test methods matching the prd-entry test_names.
Vet package line coverage is 100% (35/35 lines in VetController, 6/6 in SpecialtyGroup, confirmed by jacocoTestReport).
MockMvc is used consistently with the established project pattern (@MockitoBean VetRepository, @WebMvcTest); no new mock points beyond the sanctioned web-layer harness.
specialty() and vet() factory methods are introduced for the new tests, satisfying the factory-method requirement for post-2026-07-31 tests.
Four-phase structure is respected; no phase comments, no branching in test bodies.

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: SpecialtyGroup is a static inner class used as an immutable view-model value type, but it inherits reference equality from Object. The architecture-principles.md closed property 'equality by value' applies to all non-entity types — the persistence-entity exception explicitly excludes types the framework does not instantiate. A static inner class with no equals()/hashCode() cannot be a value object. The modern Java idiom for this shape is a record, which satisfies immutability, structural equality, and the code-quality checklist item for modern Java idioms in one step. The Javadoc comment 'Public so the Thymeleaf view can read its properties' is also misleading: the class is public because it is accessed as a model attribute type, and Spring Framework 6+ BeanWrapper resolves record accessor names (name(), veterinarians()) from Thymeleaf SpEL expressions (${group.name}, ${group.veterinarians}) — the template requires no changes.
findings.fix: Replace the static inner class with: public record SpecialtyGroup(String name, List<Vet> veterinarians) {}. Move the existing Javadoc to the record declaration. Remove the explicit constructor, field declarations, getName(), and getVeterinarians(). The package-private construction site in showSpecialtyList remains valid because records use the canonical constructor. The template expressions ${group.name} and ${group.veterinarians} continue to resolve correctly via Spring's record-aware BeanWrapper.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The comment '// dentistry is in the authoritative set but held by no veterinarian.' restates two things the code already says: the test name (theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian) and the stub arrangement (dentistry in findSpecialties(), no vet in findAll() holds it). testing-principles.md § Four-Phase Test Structure forbids prose that restates what the code already says. The other three ordering comments in the new tests are not restating — they explain a deliberate data-layout decision (out-of-alphabetical-order input to expose a hash-iteration regression) that is non-obvious and therefore permitted; this comment has no equivalent non-obvious content.

approved_aspects: All six tests pass; BUILD SUCCESSFUL; VetController line coverage 100% (35/35)

stringContainsInOrder is genuinely order-sensitive: asserting 'Amy Adams' before 'Helen Leary' when the input supplies them in reverse order (Leary id=2, Adams id=6) means a non-deterministic sort (HashSet iteration) would fail the assertion. The rendered-output assertion tests the full controller-to-template pipeline, which is the right scope for a @WebMvcTest. The implementer's rationale is sound: Hamcrest hasProperty uses java.beans.Introspector which does not resolve record component accessors (name(), veterinarians()) because records expose them without a get prefix, so hasProperty on SpecialtyGroup would silently fail to find any property. Rendered-order via stringContainsInOrder is not weaker in any way that matters for this test's regression-detection goal.

Legacy tests showVetListHtml and showResourcesVetList correctly kept under the pre-2026-07-31 naming convention. testing-principles.md § Test Naming reads: 'Applies to tests written or modified from 2026-07-31 onward. The existing suite predates this school and largely mirrors production method names; renaming it wholesale is not required, and a slice that touches a test renames only that test.' The two legacy tests were not touched by this slice, so renaming is not required. The implementer's reading is correct.

All three PRD Done-when bullets for REQ-VET-003 are covered by dedicated tests: AC1 (specialties listed with vets by full name) by theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEachSpecialtyWithVeterinariansByFullName; AC2 (no-specialty grouping) by theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty; AC3 (single page, no pagination) by theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage. The ADR authoritative-axis edge case (specialty held by no vet) is covered by theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListSpecialtyHeldByNoVeterinarian.
All four new tests follow the the{Subject}Should{Outcome} school.

theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty asserts the model attribute unspecializedVets using contains(hasProperty('lastName', is('Adams')), hasProperty('lastName', is('Baker'))). This works correctly: Vet is a JPA entity with getLastName(), so Introspector finds it. The assertion is order-sensitive and confirms the controller's BY_FULL_NAME sort applies to unspecialized vets.

Factory methods specialty(int, String) and vet(int, String, String, Specialty...) wrap all object construction in the new tests per testing-principles.md § Test Data Construction. No raw constructors in test bodies.
Four-phase structure is maintained: blank lines separate the Arrange stubs from the Act (mockMvc.perform) in all four new tests.

@MockitoBean for VetRepository is pre-existing class infrastructure from before the slice. The new tests extend that class and their stubs are the appropriate tool within a @WebMvcTest context. The brief designates MockMvc as the sanctioned mock (web transport boundary); the repository stub is tolerated per testing-principles.md § Mocking Policy: 'the existing suite stubs collaborators with a mock framework, and that usage may stay.'

The ordering rationale comments in theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListEachSpecialtyWithVeterinariansByFullName (lines 127-130), theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldGroupVeterinariansHoldingNoSpecialty (lines 146-148), and theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldRenderAllSpecialtiesOnOnePage (lines 168-170) explain a non-obvious test design decision — deliberately out-of-order input to expose a hash-iteration regression — and are not mere restatement. They comply with testing-principles.md.
